name: Cotonou Cadjehoun International Airport
before:
Benin's main airport and effectively its only international one, sitting in the Cadjehoun neighbourhood of Cotonou, the country's largest city. Flights run to destinations across Africa and to Europe.

It was renamed in 2021 after Cardinal Bernardin Gantin, so older schedules and guidebooks still list it as Cotonou Cadjehoun. Both names refer to the same place.

A replacement has been talked about for a very long time. The decision to move operations to a new site at Glo-Djigbe was taken in 1974 and ran out of funding. The plan was revived in 2011 with South African backing and a ceremonial start to construction, and appears to have stalled again since. Work has gone into improving the existing airport instead, so for the foreseeable future this remains the way into Benin.
after:
Benin's main airport and effectively its only international one, sitting in the Cadjehoun neighbourhood of Cotonou. Flights run to destinations across Africa and to Europe.

It is named after Cardinal Bernardin Gantin, but older schedules and guidebooks may still call it Cotonou Cadjehoun. Both names refer to the same place.

A replacement airport at Glo-Djigbé has long been planned, but work has gone into improving this one, and for the foreseeable future it remains the way into Benin.

claims.claim: FCDO: visa online 7 days ahead, collected at Cotonou airport; yellow fever certificate; northern warnings
claims.why: Held back: entry rules and warnings that replace nothing. The FCDO (warnings updated 15 December 2025, still current 24 September 2026) says British visitors need a visa, applied for online at least 7 days before arrival and collected at Cotonou airport, and a yellow fever vaccination certificate. It advises against all travel to the Parc du W, the Pendjari National Park and within 5 km of the Burkina Faso border, and against all but essential travel to the rest of Alibori and Atacora and near the Nigerian border in the east. Cotonou is not in those areas. Note for Andy: the airport's own home page promotes the Pendjari National Park, where the FCDO advises against all travel.
